source.check: returned unopposed: 'There will be no contest for Tyrone County Council, 15 Unionists and 12 Nationalists - the total number of the elected members - being returned unopposed' (Belfast News-Letter, 17 May 1961)

note: Triennial election of Tyrone County Council, 1961. Nominations were received on 16 May 1961: 'Names can be withdrawn up to 3 p.m. to-day and polling takes place on June 1' (Belfast News-Letter, 17 May 1961, p. 5) - Thursday 1 June 1961. There was no contest: 15 Unionists and 12 Nationalists were returned unopposed (same page). The Returning Officer's notice of result, printed in the Ulster Herald and the Strabane Chronicle of 20 May 1961, lists all 27 divisions with one candidate each, and the full council is recorded from it. Uncontested divisions here reflect a deliberate abstention, not missing coverage: in the Omagh Rural District, Nationalists refused to nominate against Unionist-held seats in every year except 1949, when only 4 of 21 such seats were contested (Kingsley 2021, 'The Omagh Rural District Electoral Divisions Scheme 1923', citing PRONI LA/62/2/FA/38 and Ulster Herald 10 Feb 1923). See notes/tyrone-county-council_absent_contests.txt Nominated for the vacancy created by the death of Mr. P. T. Devlin; the paper assigns this change to the Nationalist side, but prints no label for him. Returned unopposed.
